I. प्रत्याशित परिचालन व्यय का अनुमान लगाना

IV. उपलब्ध अनुदानों, आवंटनों और निधियों की पहचान करना

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा इन चरणों का सही तार्किक और कालानुक्रमिक क्रम दर्शाता है?

questions.question_english:
Consider the following steps in preparing and finalizing a school budget:
I. Estimation of anticipated expenditure
II. Review of previous year’s expenditure
III. Approval by the Directorate
IV. Identification of available grants and funds

Which of the following represents the correct logical sequence of these steps?
questions.explanation_english:
In financial administration and educational planning under GFR 2017 and Delhi Directorate of Education guidelines, formulating an annual school budget follows a systematic, step-by-step administrative procedure:

Step 1 - Review of previous year's expenditure (Step II):
The budgeting process begins with analyzing past financial performance, actual spending trends, historical burn rates, and examining under-utilization or over-expenditure across heads (salaries, utilities, maintenance, contingencies).

Step 2 - Identification of available grants and funds (Step IV):
Next, the school maps all expected financial inflows, revenue resources, and sanctioned scheme grants—including Samagra Shiksha grants, Vidyalaya Kalyan Samiti (VKS) funds, Free Textbook subsidies, examination grants, and pupil fund allocations.

Step 3 - Estimation of anticipated expenditure (Step I):
Based on realistic student enrollment projections, academic requirements, lab consumables, repair demands, and salary revisions, the school computes itemized budget estimates for the upcoming financial year.

Step 4 - Approval by the Directorate (Step III):
Finally, the draft budget is vetted by the School Management Committee (SMC), compiled into the prescribed budgetary formats (Budget Estimates / Revised Estimates), and submitted to the Directorate of Education / Competent Financial Authority for formal administrative vetting and financial sanction.

Thus, the correct logical and chronological sequence is II → IV → I → III, making Option (B) the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
वित्तीय प्रशासन तथा दिल्ली शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE) के वित्तीय दिशा-निर्देशों एवं GFR 2017 के तहत विद्यालय का वार्षिक बजट तैयार करने का एक तार्किक एवं कालानुक्रमिक क्रम निर्धारित है:

पहला चरण - पिछले वर्ष के व्यय की समीक्षा और विश्लेषण (चरण II):
बजट निर्माण की शुरुआत विगत वित्तीय वर्ष के वास्तविक व्यय, विभिन्न मदों (वेतन, बिजली-पानी, स्टेशनरी, आकस्मिक व्यय) में खर्च के रुझानों तथा अप्रयुक्त शेष राशि के गहन विश्लेषण से होती है।

दूसरा चरण - उपलब्ध अनुदानों, आवंटनों और निधियों की पहचान (चरण IV):
इसके उपरांत विद्यालय को आगामी वर्ष में प्राप्त होने वाले वित्तीय स्रोतों व अनुदानों की पहचान करनी होती है—जैसे समग्र शिक्षा अनुदान, विद्यालय कल्याण समिति (VKS/SMC) फंड, निःशुल्क पाठ्यपुस्तक अनुदान तथा अन्य सरकारी वित्तीय आवंटन।

तीसरा चरण - प्रत्याशित परिचालन व्यय का अनुमान लगाना (चरण I):
छात्रों के अनुमानित नामांकन, शैक्षणिक आवश्यकताओं, प्रयोगशाला उपकरण, रखरखाव तथा कर्मचारियों के वेतन वृद्धि के आधार पर आगामी वर्ष के संभावित व्यय का मदवार आकलन तैयार किया जाता है।

चौथा चरण - शिक्षा निदेशालय द्वारा प्रस्तुति और औपचारिक अनुमोदन (चरण III):
अंत में, तैयार किए गए समेकित बजट प्रस्ताव को विद्यालय प्रबंधन समिति (SMC) के अनुमोदन के उपरांत शिक्षा निदेशालय/सक्षम वित्तीय प्राधिकारी के समक्ष अंतिम प्रशासनिक समीक्षा और वित्तीय स्वीकृति हेतु प्रस्तुत किया जाता है।

अतः सही तार्किक क्रम II → IV → I → III है, जिससे विकल्प (B) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) II, IV, I, III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Preparing a school budget follows a logical administrative order starting with reviewing the previous year expenditure. Next, available grants and revenue sources are identified, followed by estimating anticipated operational expenses for the coming year. Finally, the consolidated budget draft is submitted to the Directorate for formal administrative review and approval.

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, which specific statutory rule regulates the cash equivalent of leave salary (Leave Encashment) payable to a government employee at the time of retirement or superannuation?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the **Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972**:

1. **Rule 39 (Leave Encashment on Retirement)**:
   - Regulates the grant of cash equivalent of leave salary for Earned Leave (EL) and Half Pay Leave (HPL) standing at credit to a government servant on the date of retirement upon superannuation, invalidation, or voluntary retirement.
   - The maximum aggregate ceiling of leave that can be encashed under Rule 39 is **300 days** (Earned Leave + Half Pay Leave combined, with EL being encashed first).
   - Formula for calculation: Leave Salary = [(Basic Pay + DA) / 30] * Number of unutilized days of leave (up to 300).
2. **Context of Other Rules Cited**:
   - **Rule 14**: General conditions for grant of leave / combination of leaves.
   - **Rule 43**: Maternity Leave provisions.
   - **Rule 50**: Extraordinary Leave (EOL) without allowances.
questions.explanation_hindi:
**केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (अवकाश) नियमावली, 1972 (CCS Leave Rules, 1972)** के अंतर्गत:

1. **नियम 39 (सेवानिवृत्ति पर अवकाश नकदीकरण)**:
   - अधिवर्षिता (Superannuation), स्वैच्छिक सेवानिवृत्ति (VRS) अथवा अमान्यता (Invalidation) पर सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले सरकारी कर्मचारी के खाते में जमा अर्जित अवकाश (EL) एवं अर्ध-वेतन अवकाश (HPL) के बदले नकद भुगतान (Leave Encashment) का नियमन नियम 39 द्वारा किया जाता है।
   - इसके तहत अधिकतम **300 दिनों** (अर्जित अवकाश और अर्ध-वेतन अवकाश दोनों को मिलाकर) के अवकाश नकदीकरण की वैधानिक सीमा निर्धारित है।
   - नकदीकरण की गणना सूत्र: अवकाश वेतन = [(मूल वेतन + महंगाई भत्ता) / 30] * अप्रयुक्त अवकाश दिवस (अधिकतम 300)।
2. **अन्य विकल्पों का संदर्भ**:
   - **नियम 14**: अवकाश की सामान्य शर्तें / अवकाशों का संयोजन।
   - **नियम 43**: मातृत्व अवकाश (Maternity Leave) के प्रावधान।
   - **नियम 50**: असाधारण अवकाश (EOL) के नियम।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Rule 39

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 39 of the Central Civil Services Leave Rules 1972 governs the cash equivalent of leave salary for earned leave and half pay leave at credit at the time of retirement. It sets parameters for calculating leave encashment benefits up to the statutory maximum limit of three hundred days.

questions.question_english: Which digital management portal serves as the official platform utilized by the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, for centralized online school admissions, Non-Plan student registrations, and administrative tracking in Delhi?
questions.explanation_english: The Directorate of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi, exclusively operates and maintains its official Educational Management Information System (MIS) portal at 'edudel.nic.in'. This comprehensive platform hosts the entire digital workflow for Delhi government and aided school admissions—including Non-Plan admissions for Classes VI to IX and XI, computerized lottery draws for private unaided school EWS/DG quota admissions, online School Leaving Certificate (SLC) generation, staff and teacher transfers, and school-level administrative notifications. In contrast, DIKSHA, SWAYAM, and e-Pathshala are national portals launched by the Ministry of Education / NCERT aimed at digital curriculum dissemination, open distance learning, and e-textbooks rather than Delhi state admission MIS administration.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा निदेशालय, राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली सरकार (DoE, GNCTD) द्वारा संचालित आधिकारिक वेब पोर्टल 'edudel.nic.in' है, जो दिल्ली के राजकीय एवं सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों के सम्पूर्ण शैक्षिक प्रबंधन सूचना तंत्र (MIS) का संचालन करता है। इस पोर्टल के माध्यम से नॉन-प्लान प्रवेश (कक्षा 6 से 9 और 11), निजी विद्यालयों में EWS/DG सीटों के लिए ऑनलाइन कम्प्यूटरीकृत ड्रा ऑफ लॉट्स, ऑनलाइन स्थानांतरण प्रमाण पत्र (SLC/TC) जारी करना, शिक्षक पदस्थापन तथा प्रशासनिक परिपत्रों का निर्गमन किया जाता है। विकल्प A (SWAYAM), B (DIKSHA) और C (e-Pathshala) केंद्र सरकार व NCERT द्वारा संचालित राष्ट्रीय डिजिटल शिक्षण प्लेटफॉर्म हैं, जो राज्य स्तरीय प्रशासनिक प्रवेश पोर्टल नहीं हैं।

questions.question_english: Under Rule 43-C of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the maximum cumulative period of Child Care Leave (CCL) admissible to a female government servant during her entire service career?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 43-C of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972 (introduced pursuant to the 6th Central Pay Commission and subsequently modified):

1. Total Entitlement: Female government servants and single male government servants (unmarried, widower, or divorcee) are entitled to Child Care Leave (CCL) for a maximum duration of 730 days during their entire service career.
2. Eligible Children: CCL is admissible for taking care of up to two eldest surviving children for rearing or looking after their needs, such as education, sickness, and examinations, until the child attains 18 years of age (with no age bar in the case of a child with benchmark disabilities).
3. Leave Salary Structure: Under 7th CPC revisions, 100% of leave salary is paid for the first 365 days of CCL, and 80% of leave salary is paid for the subsequent 365 days.
4. Spells: CCL may not be granted in more than 3 spells in a single calendar year, with a minimum spell duration of 5 days.
Therefore, 730 days is the maximum entitlement (Option B).
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (अवकाश) नियमावली, 1972 के नियम 43-C के अंतर्गत बाल देखभाल अवकाश (Child Care Leave - CCL) के प्रमुख वैधानिक प्रावधान निम्नलिखित हैं:

1. कुल स्वीकार्य अवधि: महिला सरकारी सेवकों तथा एकल पुरुष सरकारी कर्मचारियों (अविवाहित, विधुर या तलाकशुदा) को उनकी संपूर्ण सेवाकाल के दौरान अधिकतम 730 दिनों (2 वर्ष) का बाल देखभाल अवकाश प्रदान किया जा सकता है।
2. बच्चों की पात्रता: यह अवकाश अधिकतम दो ज्येष्ठ जीवित बच्चों के पालन-पोषण, शिक्षा, बीमारी अथवा परीक्षा संबंधी आवश्यकताओं की देखभाल हेतु 18 वर्ष की आयु तक (दिव्यांग बच्चों के मामले में कोई आयु सीमा नहीं) अनुमेय है।
3. अवकाश वेतन: 7वें वेतन आयोग की अनुशंसाओं के अनुसार, पहले 365 दिनों हेतु 100% अवकाश वेतन तथा अगले 365 दिनों हेतु 80% अवकाश वेतन देय होता है।
4. वार्षिक सीमा: एक कैलेंडर वर्ष में CCL सामान्यतः अधिकतम 3 स्पेल (Spells) में दिया जा सकता है, तथा न्यूनतम स्पेल 5 दिनों से कम का नहीं होना चाहिए।
अतः सही उत्तर 730 दिन (विकल्प B) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 730 days

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Female government servants are eligible for Child Care Leave for a maximum duration of seven hundred thirty days during their entire service period. This leave is granted for taking care of up to two eldest surviving children for rearing or looking after needs such as education or illness under prescribed conditions.

questions.question_english: Under the provisions of the Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSEAR), 1973 and orders of the High Court of Delhi, which committee is responsible for examining disputes and fee structures in recognized private unaided schools in Delhi when grievances arise?
questions.explanation_english:
In NCT of Delhi, private unaided recognized schools are governed by Section 17(3) and Rules 172-180 of the Delhi School Education Act & Rules (DSEAR), 1973, which mandate that schools shall not indulge in the commercialization of education or charging of capitation fees.

1. **Fee Anomaly Committee (FAC)**:
   - Pursuant to landmark Delhi High Court directions (including the Justice Anil Dev Singh Committee recommendations and Modern School v. Union of India), the Directorate of Education constituted a district-level **Fee Anomaly Committee** headed by the Deputy Director of Education (District) along with a Chartered Accountant and education officers.
   - **Mandate**: Examines complaints submitted by parents, Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), or guardians against arbitrary, unilateral fee increases, capitation fees, or diversion of school funds by private school managements.
   - **Enforcement**: If the committee finds that a fee hike is unjustified, it directs the management to refund/adjust the excess fees collected and recommends withdrawal of recognition under DSEAR 1973 in cases of persistent non-compliance.
questions.explanation_hindi:
राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली में मान्यता प्राप्त निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालय दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम एवं नियमावली (DSEAR), 1973 की धारा 17(3) तथा नियम 172 से 180 के अंतर्गत विनियमित होते हैं, जो शिक्षा के व्यावसायीकरण और कैपिटेशन फीस लेने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध लगाते हैं।

1. **फी एनोमली कमेटी (Fee Anomaly Committee - शुल्क विसंगति समिति)**:
   - दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय के ऐतिहासिक निर्देशों (जस्टिस अनिल देव सिंह समिति की रिपोर्ट तथा मॉडर्न स्कूल बनाम भारत संघ) के अनुपालन में जिला स्तर पर उप-शिक्षा निदेशक (DDE - जिला) की अध्यक्षता में 'फी एनोमली कमेटी' का गठन किया जाता है, जिसमें चार्टर्ड अकाउंटेंट और शिक्षा अधिकारी शामिल होते हैं।
   - **कार्य एवं अधिकार**: यह समिति निजी स्कूल प्रबंधन द्वारा की गई अनुचित अथवा एकतरफा फीस वृद्धि, गैर-कानूनी फंड ट्रांसफर तथा अभिभावकों द्वारा दर्ज की गई वित्तीय शिकायतों की जांच करती है।
   - **निर्णय**: जांच में फीस वृद्धि अनुचित पाए जाने पर विद्यालय को बढ़ाई गई अतिरिक्त फीस वापस या समायोजित करने का आदेश दिया जाता है, और अनुपालन न करने पर मान्यता रद्द करने की सिफारिश की जा सकती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Fee Anomaly Committee

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When disputes regarding fee hikes or financial irregularities occur in private unaided schools in Delhi, the Fee Anomaly Committee acts as the designated statutory body to examine complaints. Constituted at the district level, it reviews school financial accounts, evaluates fee justification, and orders rectifications to prevent commercialization.

questions.question_hindi: शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE), राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली सरकार के edudel.nic.in पोर्टल पर विभाग के विरुद्ध दायर कानूनी वादों (न्यायालयी मामलों) के प्रभावी प्रबंधन एवं निगरानी हेतु एक समर्पित ऑनलाइन मॉड्यूल उपलब्ध है। इस मॉड्यूल का आधिकारिक नाम क्या है?

questions.question_english: The edudel.nic.in portal of the Directorate of Education (DoE), GNCT of Delhi, features a dedicated online module for tracking and managing court litigations filed against the department. What is the official nomenclature of this module?
questions.explanation_english:
Under the e-governance framework of the Directorate of Education (DoE), Government of NCT of Delhi, the dedicated module hosted on the official portal (edudel.nic.in) for managing legal affairs is known as the **Legal Court Case Monitoring System (LCCMS)**.

Key aspects of LCCMS include:
1. **Litigation Tracking**: Delhi Government schools and the DoE face various litigations across the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Delhi High Court, Supreme Court of India, and District/Labour Courts regarding service matters, admissions (EWS/DG, general seats), school fee regulation, and land/infrastructure issues.
2. **Compliance & Timelines**: LCCMS allows the Legal Branch, DDEs (District/Zone), and Heads of Schools (HoS) to upload case details, track court dates, assign government counsels/advocates, upload counter-affidavits/written statements, and monitor compliance of judicial directions within stipulated deadlines.
3. **Alerts & Accountability**: The system generates automated alerts for upcoming hearings to prevent contempt of court proceedings and ensures accountability of nodal officers handling departmental legal matters.

questions.question_english: Which statutory register maintains the comprehensive history, procurement cost, inventory count, and physical verification record of non-consumable infrastructure assets like furniture, fixtures, laboratory instruments, and computers in a school?
options_english: Property Register (Dead Stock Register / Form GFR-22)
questions.explanation_english:
Under General Financial Rules (GFR 2017, Rules 238–242) and Rule 164 of the Delhi School Education Rules (DSER), 1973, educational institutions must maintain distinct statutory inventory registers:
1. Property Register / Dead Stock Register (Form GFR-22 / GFR-40): A permanent statutory ledger that documents all capital, non-consumable, and durable infrastructure assets (e.g., student dual desks, steel almirahs, laboratory equipment, desktop computers, smart boards, and water coolers). It captures the acquisition date, purchase voucher number, supplier name, quantity, unit cost, location in the school, and physical condition during mandatory annual verification.
2. Consumable Stock Register (Form GFR-23): Records perishable or expendable stores consumed during regular school operations (stationery, registers, lab chemicals, chalk).
3. Cash Book: Records daily receipts and payments of government and student fund monies.
Hence, the Property/Dead Stock Register is the mandatory record for infrastructure assets.
questions.explanation_hindi:

1. संपत्ति रजिस्टर / डेड स्टॉक रजिस्टर (Property Register / Dead Stock Register - Form GFR-22): यह एक स्थायी वैधानिक अभिलेख है जिसमें विद्यालय की सभी गैर-उपभोज्य (non-consumable) एवं पूंजीगत परिसंपत्तियों जैसे विद्यार्थियों के डेस्क, स्टील अलमारियां, साइंस लैब उपकरण, कंप्यूटर, प्रोजेक्टर, वाटर कूलर आदि का पूर्ण विवरण दर्ज किया जाता है। इसमें क्रय तिथि, बिल संख्या, विक्रेता का नाम, मात्रा, मूल्य तथा अनिवार्य वार्षिक भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) का विवरण दर्ज होता है।
2. उपभोज्य स्टॉक रजिस्टर (Consumable Register - Form GFR-23): इसमें उपभोग की जाने वाली दैनिक सामग्री जैसे स्टेशनरी, चाक, रसायन, खेलकूद उपभोज्य आदि का विवरण होता है।
3. रोकड़ बही (Cash Book): इसमें दैनिक नकद प्राप्तियों और व्यय का हिसाब रखा जाता है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Property Register (Dead Stock Register)

It tracks details of furniture, laboratory equipment, computers, fixtures, and administrative hardware, recording acquisition dates, quantities, costs, and physical condition for audit verification.

questions.explanation_english:
Following landmark child safety directives issued by the Supreme Court of India, NCPCR, and Directorate of Education (DoE) Delhi in compliance with the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012**:

1. **Coverage of Blind Spots**: Schools must eliminate unmonitored zones by installing high-definition CCTV cameras covering all student-accessible 'blind spots', including stairwells, corridors, playground perimeters, drinking water stations, basements, and outside washroom entrance areas (while strictly preserving privacy inside washrooms and changing rooms).
2. **Access & Storage**: Continuous CCTV footage recording with minimum storage retention (typically 30 to 60 days) must be maintained under the direct supervision of the Head of School (HoS) / designated Security In-Charge.
3. **Safety Audits**: The School Safety Committee and SMC must conduct monthly safety audits to ensure that no new blind spots emerge due to construction, foliage growth, or equipment relocation.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4 and Section 14(2) of the RTE Act, 2009, read with Directorate of Education guidelines regarding Out-of-School Children (OoSC) and Non-Plan admissions: (1) Section 14(2) explicitly provides that 'no child shall be denied admission in a school for lack of age proof'; (2) Section 15 mandates that no child shall be denied admission on grounds of late application; (3) Section 4 guarantees that an out-of-school child shall be admitted in a class appropriate to his or her age. The school must then conduct a baseline assessment of Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) and provide Special Training under Samagra Shiksha to enable the child to achieve parity with the age-appropriate class without denying educational access.
questions.explanation_hindi: RTE अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 14(2) स्पष्ट निर्देश देती है कि 'किसी भी बच्चे को आयु के प्रमाण के अभाव में विद्यालय में प्रवेश से वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा।' इसके अतिरिक्त धारा 4 के अनुसार शाला-त्यागी या कभी स्कूल न गए बच्चे को उसकी आयु-अनुरूप कक्षा (Age-appropriate class) में प्रवेश दिया जाएगा तथा उसे सामान्य सहपाठियों के स्तर पर लाने हेतु विशेष प्रशिक्षण (Special Training) दिया जाएगा। DoE के परिपत्रों के अनुसार, विद्यालय प्रमुख (Principal) को अभिभावक द्वारा प्रस्तुत सादे कागज पर आयु की स्व-घोषणा के आधार पर बच्चे को तुरंत अनंतिम (provisional) प्रवेश देना होगा। तत्पश्चात बच्चे की बुनियादी साक्षरता और संख्यात्मक दक्षता (FLN) का मूल्यांकन कर उसे कक्षा 6 में उपयुक्त सहायता प्रदान की जाएगी। किसी भी परिस्थिति में छात्र को प्रवेश से मना नहीं किया जा सकता।

questions.question_english: Under Rule 32 of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, which specific category of leave is sanctioned strictly at the discretion of the leave sanctioning authority when no other leave is admissible under the rules?
options_english: Leave Not Due under exceptional circumstances
Half Pay Leave on private affairs
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 32 of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, Extraordinary Leave (EOL) is granted under specific statutory conditions:

1. Discretionary Grounds: EOL may be granted to a government servant:
   (a) when no other leave is admissible under the rules, or
   (b) when other leave is admissible, but the government servant applies in writing for the grant of extraordinary leave.
2. Discretion of Authority: The grant of EOL is strictly at the discretion of the competent leave sanctioning authority and cannot be claimed as a matter of right.
3. Financial Consequence: A government servant on Extraordinary Leave is not entitled to any leave salary (without pay). Furthermore, EOL taken without medical grounds generally does not count as qualifying service for increments or pension unless specifically relaxed under Fundamental Rules (FR 26).
4. Contrast with Leave Not Due (Rule 31): 'Leave Not Due' is an advance debit against future Half Pay Leave credits granted only on medical grounds or to permanent employees, not a purely discretionary leave granted when no leave is admissible. Hence, Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:

3. वित्तीय प्रभाव: असाधारण अवकाश की अवधि के दौरान कर्मचारी को कोई अवकाश वेतन (No pay and allowances) नहीं मिलता। चिकित्सा प्रमाण पत्र के बिना लिया गया EOL वेतनवृद्धि या पेंशन के लिए अर्हक सेवा (Qualifying Service) में भी नहीं गिना जाता।
4. अदेय अवकाश (Leave Not Due) से अंतर: अदेय अवकाश (नियम 31) भविष्य में अर्जित होने वाले अर्ध-वेतन अवकाश (HPL) के विरुद्ध अग्रिम रूप से चिकित्सा आधार पर दिया जाता है।

questions.question_english: A core constitutional and pedagogical objective of the PM POSHAN (formerly Mid-Day Meal) Scheme is fostering social equity and eliminating caste prejudices. How is this mandate practically implemented during meal distribution in schools?
options_english: Serving specialized dietary meals tailored to individual caste or social background

questions.explanation_english:
The **Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN)** Scheme (governed by National Food Security Act, 2013 and Ministry of Education guidelines) serves two foundational purposes: enhancing child nutrition/school enrollment and actively building **social equity**.

Practical implementation parameters in Delhi schools:
1. **Commensality (Eating Together)**: All students, irrespective of caste, religion, creed, gender, or socio-economic background, sit together in a common line (*pangat*) or dining hall and partake of the exact same wholesome meal prepared as per prescribed nutritional standards.
2. **Eradication of Social Distinctions**: Segregated seating or differential treatment based on caste or social identity is strictly prohibited and constitutes a punishable offense.
3. **Engagement of Cook-cum-Helpers**: Guidelines specifically prioritize the appointment of Cook-cum-Helpers from marginalized communities (SC, ST, OBC, minority women, and single mothers), reinforcing inclusivity and dignity of labor within the school community.

questions.question_english: Which specific section of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973 governs the terms and conditions of service of employees in recognized private schools, stipulating that their scales of pay, allowances, and other retirement benefits shall not be less than those of employees in corresponding government schools?
questions.explanation_english:
Section 10(1) of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973 is a cornerstone statutory provision ensuring parity of service conditions for private school staff. It explicitly provides:
'The scales of pay and allowances, medical facilities, pension, gratuity, provident fund and other prescribed benefits of the employees of a recognized private school shall not be less than those of the employees of the corresponding status in schools run by the appropriate authority.'

Key implications and judicial rulings:
1. Statutory Pay Parity: Section 10 mandates that private unaided recognized school managements must grant pay scales, dearness allowance, and Central Pay Commission (CPC) revisions (such as the 6th and 7th CPC) equivalent to teachers in Delhi Government schools.
2. Enforceability: The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and the Supreme Court of India have repeatedly held that private school managements cannot plead financial incapacity to evade compliance with Section 10. Non-compliance empowers the Directorate of Education (DoE) to take over school management or withdraw recognition under Sections 20 and 24.
3. Comparison with other sections: Section 4 deals with the recognition of schools; Section 8 relates to terms and conditions of service (protection against arbitrary dismissal/removal without prior approval of the Director); Section 15 governs contracts of service.

Therefore, Section 10 is the governing statutory provision.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम (DSEA), 1973 की धारा 10(1) एक ऐतिहासिक वैधानिक प्रावधान है जो मान्यता प्राप्त निजी स्कूलों के कर्मचारियों के वेतन एवं सेवा शर्तों की सुरक्षा करता है।

धारा 10(1) के मुख्य प्रावधान:
1. वैधानिक वेतन समानता: धारा 10(1) में स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लिखित है कि किसी मान्यता प्राप्त निजी विद्यालय के कर्मचारियों के वेतनमान, भत्ते, चिकित्सा सुविधाएं, पेंशन, उपदान (ग्रेच्युटी), भविष्य निधि और अन्य निर्धारित लाभ, समुचित प्राधिकरण (दिल्ली सरकार/स्थानीय निकाय) द्वारा संचालित विद्यालयों के समान पद वाले कर्मचारियों से किसी भी प्रकार कम नहीं होंगे।
2. 7वें वेतन आयोग का अनिवार्य क्रियान्वयन: निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों को भी सरकारी शिक्षकों की भांति केंद्रीय वेतन आयोग (जैसे 7th CPC) के अनुसार वेतनमान व भत्ते देना कानूनन अनिवार्य है।
3. न्यायिक स्थिति: दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय तथा सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने अनेक निर्णयों में यह स्पष्ट किया है कि निजी स्कूल वित्तीय असमर्थता का बहाना बनाकर धारा 10 के अनुपालन से बच नहीं सकते। इसका उल्लंघन करने पर शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE) को अधिनियम की धारा 20 और 24 के तहत स्कूल प्रबंधन का अधिग्रहण करने अथवा मान्यता रद्द करने का अधिकार है।
4. अन्य धाराएं: धारा 4 विद्यालयों की मान्यता से, धारा 8 कर्मचारियों की सेवा सुरक्षा (बर्खास्तगी/निलंबन पर निदेशक की पूर्व अनुमति) से, तथा धारा 15 सेवा अनुबंध से संबंधित है।

अतः सही उत्तर धारा 10 (Section 10) है।

questions.question_english: Which compensatory allowance is specifically granted to government employees and pensioners to insulate their real income against the rising cost of living index and price inflation?
questions.explanation_english: Dearness Allowance (DA) is a cost-of-living compensatory allowance paid to serving Central/State Government employees, while Dearness Relief (DR) is paid to pensioners. It is computed as a percentage of basic pay to offset the erosion of real purchasing power caused by inflation. The Government of India reviews and revises DA twice a year (effective from 1st January and 1st July) using the 12-month average of the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW). HRA compensates for residential accommodation expenses, and Transport Allowance compensates for commuting expenses.
questions.explanation_hindi: महंगाई भत्ता (Dearness Allowance - DA) सेवारत सरकारी कर्मचारियों को और महंगाई राहत (DR) पेंशनभोगियों को मुद्रास्फीति और जीवन यापन की लागत में वृद्धि के प्रभाव को कम करने के लिए दिया जाने वाला भत्ता है। यह मूल वेतन के एक निश्चित प्रतिशत के रूप में देय होता है। भारत सरकार द्वारा औद्योगिक श्रमिकों के लिए अखिल भारतीय उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकांक (AICPI-IW) के आधार पर प्रतिवर्ष दो बार (1 जनवरी और 1 जुलाई से प्रभावी) महंगाई भत्ते की दरों में संशोधन किया जाता है। मकान किराया भत्ता (HRA) आवास व्यय और परिवहन भत्ता आवागमन व्यय हेतु दिया जाता है।

questions.question_english: As mandated by Rule 149 of GFR 2017 for all government institutions and Directorate of Education (DoE) schools, what is the primary objective of procuring goods and services through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?
options_english: To generate non-tax commercial revenue for Central and State Governments
To ensure transparency, efficiency, and speed in public procurement
To disburse collateral-free credit and short-term working loans to registered suppliers
To circumvent internal statutory audits and procedural accounting compliance
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017, public procurement of commonly used goods and services is mandatorily routed through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal developed by the Directorate General of Supplies and Disposals (DGS&D) / Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The overarching objective of GeM is to promote transparency, operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and speed in public procurement across government departments, autonomous bodies, and Delhi government schools. GeM eliminates physical bureaucratic interfaces, facilitates cashless and paperless e-bidding/reverse auction, enables direct market price discovery, and provides real-time tracking from purchase requisition to end-to-end payment.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियमावली (GFR) 2017 के नियम 149 के अंतर्गत, सरकारी विभागों, स्वायत्त निकायों तथा दिल्ली सरकार के विद्यालयों द्वारा सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की खरीद अनिवार्य रूप से गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) पोर्टल के माध्यम से की जानी चाहिए। GeM का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक खरीद (Public Procurement) में संपूर्ण पारदर्शिता, कार्यकुशलता, मितव्ययिता और गति सुनिश्चित करना है। यह पोर्टल बिचौलियों को समाप्त कर डिजिटल माध्यम से रिवर्स ऑक्शन और सीधी खरीद की सुविधा प्रदान करता है, जिससे निष्पक्ष प्रतिस्पर्धा, वास्तविक मूल्य खोज (price discovery) और समयबद्ध ऑनलाइन भुगतान संभव होता है।

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Principal of a Delhi Government school cannot deduct the salary of an employee as a penalty without following the procedure laid down in the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965.

questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

1. **Statutory Framework under CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 & DSEAR, 1973**:
   - Under Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, penal recovery of any pecuniary loss caused to the Government, withholding of increments, or reduction to a lower stage/pay constitute statutory penalties (minor or major penalties).

2. **Principles of Natural Justice**:
   - Deducting salary without observing due process violates the fundamental constitutional doctrine of audi alteram partem (hear the other side) and Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India. Hence, Reason (R) directly explains why Assertion (A) is legally binding.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4 and Section 3 of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973 (DSEAR 1973), read with Rule 56 of the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973, the 'appropriate authority' is the Director of Education (DoE), GNCTD (or an officer authorized on their behalf). The Director of Education is vested with statutory authority to grant, regulate, suspend, or withdraw the recognition of any private unaided or aided school in the National Capital Territory of Delhi. Withdrawal of recognition (de-recognition) is initiated when a school breaches the terms and conditions of recognition, persistently violates statutory fee norms, fails to comply with admission guidelines (including mandatory 25% EWS/DG admissions under RTE Section 12(1)(c)), fails to pay salaries according to the prescribed pay scales under Section 10(1), or compromises student safety and infrastructure. Before de-recognition, the Director must issue a show-cause notice and provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

questions.question_english: In the case of admissions under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) / Disadvantaged Group (DG) category, if a private unaided recognized school refuses admission to an allotted student on the pretext of lack of infrastructure, what is the statutory consequence under Delhi school education laws?

The school becomes eligible for infrastructure development grants from state government funds.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, read with the statutory provisions of the Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSEAR), 1973, private unaided recognized schools are legally bound to admit at least 25% children from EWS/DG categories at the entry level through the Directorate of Education's centralized computerized lottery.

Statutory Consequences of Refusal:
1. Unconditional Admission Requirement: Once a candidate is allotted a seat by the Directorate of Education (DoE), the school cannot deny admission on grounds of infrastructure deficiencies, teacher shortage, or delay in government reimbursement. Any such pretext is treated as willful defiance of statutory directives.
2. Enforcement under DSEAR 1973: Under Section 4 and Section 24 of DSEAR, 1973, the Director of Education has statutory powers to issue show-cause notices, withdraw recognition (de-recognition), or recommend the takeover of the school's management under Section 20 for non-compliance with admission mandates.
3. Land Allotment Conditions: Most private unaided schools in Delhi were allotted institutional land by DDA/L&DO at concessional rates with the mandatory condition to provide free education to EWS students. Refusal also violates land allotment lease conditions, risking lease cancellation.

Hence, the school faces penal action, including de-recognition under DSEAR 1973.

शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 12(1)(c) तथा दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम एवं नियम (DSEAR), 1973 के वैधानिक प्रावधानों के अंतर्गत सभी निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त मान्यता प्राप्त विद्यालयों के लिए प्रवेश स्तर (Entry Level) की 25% सीटें ईडब्ल्यूएस/डीजी (EWS/DG) वर्ग के बच्चों हेतु आरक्षित रखना और शिक्षा निदेशालय द्वारा केंद्रीकृत कम्प्यूटरीकृत ड्रॉ के माध्यम से आवंटित छात्रों को प्रवेश देना अनिवार्य है।

प्रवेश से इनकार के कानूनी परिणाम:
1. कोई बहाना स्वीकार्य नहीं: विद्यालय प्रशासन अवसंरचना की कमी, सीटों की अनुपलब्धता या वित्तीय बाधाओं का बहाना बनाकर शिक्षा निदेशालय द्वारा आवंटित छात्र को प्रवेश देने से मना नहीं कर सकता।
2. DSEAR 1973 के तहत दंडात्मक कार्यवाही: दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम, 1973 की धारा 4 और 24 के अंतर्गत, विभागीय निर्देशों का उल्लंघन करने पर शिक्षा निदेशक को विद्यालय की मान्यता समाप्त (De-recognition) करने, अनापत्ति प्रमाण पत्र (NOC) वापस लेने, तथा धारा 20 के तहत विद्यालय प्रबंधन का अधिग्रहण करने तक की शक्ति प्राप्त है।
3. रियायती भूमि की शर्तें: दिल्ली में अधिकांश निजी विद्यालयों को DDA द्वारा रियायती दरों पर भूमि इसी शर्त पर आवंटित की गई थी कि वे निर्धन वर्ग के बच्चों को निःशुल्क शिक्षा देंगे। प्रवेश से इनकार करना पट्टा विलेख (Lease Deed) का भी गंभीर उल्लंघन है।

questions.question_english: Under the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the statutory ceiling on the accumulation of Earned Leave (EL) that a government servant can maintain at their credit?
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 26 of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, the rules governing Earned Leave (EL) for civilian government servants are as follows:

1. Annual Credit: Government servants working in non-vacation establishments earn 30 days of EL each year, credited in advance in two equal installments of 15 days on the 1st of January and 1st of July.
2. Maximum Accumulation Limit: The maximum limit of Earned Leave that can be accumulated and carried forward at credit is three hundred (300) days.
3. Buffer for Advance Credit: While an additional advance credit of up to 15 days can be shown in a separate buffer column during the transition of half-years (up to 300+15 days), the permanent statutory accumulation ceiling remains strictly 300 days.
4. Encashment at Retirement: Upon retirement or superannuation under Rule 39, leave encashment is paid up to a maximum ceiling of 300 days of accumulated leave.
Therefore, Option C (300 days) is the correct answer.

1. वार्षिक क्रेडिट: गैर-अवकाश (Non-vacation) विभागों में कार्यरत कर्मचारियों के अवकाश खाते में प्रति वर्ष 30 दिनों का अर्जित अवकाश दो किश्तों में (1 जनवरी और 1 जुलाई को 15-15 दिन) अग्रिम रूप से जमा किया जाता है।

3. सेवानिवृत्ति पर नकदीकरण (Leave Encashment): नियम 39 के तहत अधिवर्षिता (Superannuation) अथवा सेवानिवृत्ति के समय अधिकतम 300 दिनों के संचित अवकाश (EL और HPL को मिलाकर, नियमानुसार) का ही नकद भुगतान किया जा सकता है।

questions.question_english: A Central Government employee is transferred from another state to Delhi in the month of November. The parent approaches a Delhi Government school seeking mid-session admission for their child in Class VIII. In accordance with the Delhi School Admission Guidelines and statutory provisions, how should the School Principal handle this admission request?
options_english: Grant admission immediately pursuant to Section 15 of the RTE Act, which prohibits denial of elementary admission anytime during the academic year
Strictly deny admission because mid-session Non-Plan admissions after the month of April are prohibited by rules
Grant provisional admission only upon payment of a prescribed late admission penalty fee by the parent
Deny admission for the current session and advise the parent to re-apply during the next academic year's regular registration
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 15 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, a child shall be admitted in a school at the commencement of the academic year, or within such extended period as may be prescribed, provided that no child shall be denied admission if such admission is sought subsequent to the extended period. Since Class VIII falls squarely within the definition of elementary education (Classes I to VIII, ages 6 to 14 years), admission cannot be denied at any time during the academic session. Furthermore, under the Directorate of Education (DoE) Delhi Non-Plan Admission Guidelines, transferred government employees and genuine relocation cases are accorded mid-session admission directly or through the concerned Deputy Director of Education (DDE) Zone/District. Charging any late admission fee or penalty is strictly prohibited under Section 13 of the RTE Act. Therefore, the Principal must grant admission without administrative hindrance.

questions.question_english: Under which section of the Delhi School Education Act (DSEA), 1973 is the Administrator empowered to regulate fees and other charges levied by recognized schools in order to prevent the commercialization and profiteering in education?
questions.explanation_english: Section 17 of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973 explicitly governs 'Fees and other charges'. Under Section 17(1), no aided school shall levy any fee or charge without previous approval of the Director. Under Section 17(3), the manager of every recognized unaided school must file with the Director a full statement of fees to be levied by such school during the ensuing academic session before the commencement of each academic year, and no school shall charge fees in excess of those notified. The Administrator / Directorate of Education uses Section 17 powers, affirmed in landmark Supreme Court judgments (e.g., Modern School v. Union of India, 2004), to audit school accounts, prevent capitation fees, prohibit commercialization and profiteering, and restrict unauthorized mid-session fee hikes. For reference: Section 4 deals with Recognition of Schools; Section 10 deals with Salaries and allowances of employees; and Section 24 deals with Inspection of Schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा अधिनियम (DSEA), 1973 की धारा 17 'फीस और अन्य शुल्क' (Fees and other charges) के नियमन से संबंधित है। धारा 17(3) के अनुसार प्रत्येक मान्यता प्राप्त गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालय के प्रबंधक को आगामी शैक्षणिक सत्र प्रारंभ होने से पूर्व ली जाने वाली फीस का संपूर्ण विवरण शिक्षा निदेशक के समक्ष प्रस्तुत करना होता है तथा कोई भी विद्यालय अधिसूचित फीस से अधिक शुल्क नहीं ले सकता। धारा 17 प्रशासक/शिक्षा निदेशालय को विद्यालयों के वित्तीय खातों का ऑडिट करने, अनुचित फीस वृद्धि रोकने तथा शिक्षा के व्यावसायीकरण (Commercialization/Profiteering) को प्रतिबंधित करने की वैधानिक शक्ति प्रदान करती है। (संदर्भ: धारा 4 = विद्यालयों की मान्यता; धारा 10 = कर्मचारियों के वेतन और भत्ते; धारा 24 = विद्यालयों का निरीक्षण)।
